title: Canva PDF Rejected for Print? Fix RGB Color and Rich Black (KDP & IngramSpark) | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix a Canva PDF that's rejected for color
description: Canva files are made in screen color, so black text can turn into four inks. Here's how to export a Canva book file the printer accepts.
lead: Canva is the go-to for book covers. But its files start in screen color, and that trips up printers.
errorNote: Paraphrased. An ink coverage over 240% message often comes with it.
why:
Canva designs in RGB, the color of screens. Printers use CMYK ink. When RGB black is turned into ink, it often becomes a "rich black" that mixes all four inks.

That causes two problems. A black-and-white interior is only allowed black ink, so any color fails. And dark areas can pass IngramSpark's 240% total ink limit, which gets the file rejected.
manual: In Canva, choose Share → Download → PDF Print.
Turn on "Crop marks and bleed" only if your printer asks for bleed in the file, and pick CMYK under Color profile if your plan shows it.
Make black text and lines plain black, not a dark photo or gradient.
Open the PDF in Acrobat Pro and check Print Production → Output Preview for RGB and for areas over 240% total ink.
Re-upload it to your printer and wait for the file review again. If it fails, you start over.
quickfix: SparkPrep finds the RGB color and over-limit ink in your Canva file, converts it to print color within the 240% limit, and exports a PDF/X-1a.

faq.q: Is Canva's PDF Print good enough for KDP?
faq.a: It can be, if the size and bleed are right. Color is the usual problem, so check for RGB and rich black before uploading.
Black made from several inks mixed together instead of black ink alone. It can break ink limits and isn't allowed in black-and-white books.
